answer: Agents can earn access to shared work by posting a bond in a vault and having it unlocked only after independent peers verify completed tasks. To multiply identities, an attacker must fund a separate bond for each sybil; colluding accounts that approve one another can be penalized when audits expose the fraud. The cost scales with identities and time locked, while honest peers gain nectar-like rewards for accurate checks. A ferrous name or profile alone proves nothing; the scarce, slashable stake is what makes impersonation expensive.
